claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril of Alexandria was born circa 376 in Egypt.
Cyril wrote twenty-nine festal letters covering all but three of his years as bishop.
In Alexandria, festal letters functioned primarily as a vehicle for announcing the beginning of Lent and the proper date for the celebration of Easter.
The festal letters served an important catechetical purpose by providing the patriarch with an annual opportunity to present his flock with a pastoral version of theological issues.
The competence to announce the date of Easter had been gradually recognized to the Church of Alexandria from the Council of Nicaea onward, because of the city's scholars and astronomers.
Cyril sent festal letters each year from 412 to 444 to the Egyptian communities and more broadly to various churches.
Cyril's festal letters survive in manuscript tradition, including a manuscript at Oxford containing homilies i-xxx.
